title: The integral chain interval gives tensor cylinders
statement: Let $\mathcal N$ be a complete and cocomplete category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded cochain complexes of abelian groups, with the complex adjunctions and ordinary morphisms given by degree-zero cycles as in [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. Suppose $\mathcal N$ has a model structure with functorial factorizations and satisfies the enriched model axiom: for a cofibration $A\to B$ and a fibration $U\to V$, the map $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,U)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,U)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,V)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,V)$ is degreewise surjective and is a quasi-isomorphism if either given map is a weak equivalence. Cofibrant means that the initial map is a cofibration. Let $J$ be the cochain complex with $J^{-1}=\mathbf Z h$, $J^0=\mathbf Z e_0\oplus\mathbf Z e_1$, $dh=e_1-e_0$, and all other terms zero. Let $j_i:\mathbf Z[0]\to J$ send $1$ to $e_i$, and let $p:J\to\mathbf Z[0]$ send $e_0,e_1$ to $1$ and $h$ to zero. In the projective model structure on complexes [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], $J$ is cofibrant, $(j_0,j_1):\mathbf Z[0]\oplus\mathbf Z[0]\to J$ is a cofibration, and $p$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For every cofibrant $X\in\mathcal N$, the maps $i_i=j_i\otimes1_X:X\to J\otimes X$ and $p_X=p\otimes1_X:J\otimes X\to X$, using the tensor unit identifications, form a good cylinder: $p_Xi_0=p_Xi_1=1_X$, $p_X$ is a weak equivalence, and $(i_0,i_1):X\amalg X\to J\otimes X$ is a cofibration. No fibrancy assumption on $X$ is imposed.

external.document: Bertrand Toën, The homotopy theory of dg-categories and derived Morita theory, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337
external.place: Section 3, Proposition 3.2, hypothesis (2), and its proof; read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Put $u=e_1-e_0$ and $v=e_0$. These form an integral basis of $J^0$, and $dh=u$, so $J=\mathbf Z v[0]\oplus D^{-1}$ as complexes, with $D^{-1}=(\mathbf Z h\xrightarrow{1}\mathbf Z u)$ in degrees $-1,0$. The degree $-1$ map $s$ on this disk, given by $s(u)=h$ and $s(h)=0$, satisfies $ds+sd=1$. For any complex $A$, its Hom complex from the disk is contractible: for a homogeneous map $f$ of degree $r$, set $H(f)=(-1)^r f s$; the Hom differential gives $dH(f)+H(df)=f(ds+sd)=f$. Also $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathbf Z[0],A)=A$, and Hom from the sphere $S^{-1}$ (the complex $\mathbf Z$ in degree $-1$ and zero elsewhere) is a shift of $A$. Hence $D^{-1}$, $\mathbf Z[0]$, $S^{-1}$ and $J$ are dg-projective by the definition in [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]: their terms are free, and Hom into an acyclic complex is acyclic. For $J$ the Hom complex is the binary direct sum of the two Hom complexes just computed. In particular $J$ is cofibrant by that node's cofibration criterion applied to $0\to J$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison; extracted chain-interval foundation. Agent proof: Integral basis change and explicit disk contraction.

proof.text: Write $c=(j_0,j_1):\mathbf Z[0]\oplus\mathbf Z[0]\to J$. In degree zero $c$ is the isomorphism taking the two standard basis vectors to $e_0,e_1$; in degree $-1$ its source is zero. Thus $c$ is a degreewise split injection with cokernel $S^{-1}$, which is dg-projective by Step 1, so $c$ is a cofibration by [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. Similarly $j_0$ is a degreewise split injection, and its cokernel has generators $h$ in degree $-1$ and the class of $e_1$ in degree zero with differential $h\mapsto e_1$; it is $D^{-1}$. Therefore $j_0$ is a cofibration. In the decomposition of Step 1, $j_0$ includes the first summand and $p$ projects onto it; the other summand is contractible, so both maps induce isomorphisms on cohomology. The projective model has quasi-isomorphisms as weak equivalences, hence $j_0$ is a trivial cofibration and $p$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison; extracted chain-interval foundation. Agent proof: The two endpoint maps and augmentation in the projective complex model.

proof.text: Denote the initial object of $\mathcal N$ by $O$. The complex adjunctions and degree-zero-cycle convention of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] imply $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(O,Y)=0$ for every $Y$: chain maps $D^n\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(O,Y)$ correspond to ordinary maps $O\to Y^{D^n}$, of which there is exactly one; a chain map from $D^n$ is determined by an arbitrary element in degree $n$ of its target. Thus each degree has one element. For fixed $X$, the tensor adjunction also identifies $(\mathbf Z[0]\oplus\mathbf Z[0])\otimes X$ with $X\amalg X$: maps from the former into $Y$ are pairs of chain maps $\mathbf Z[0]\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y)$, namely pairs of ordinary maps $X\to Y$. The resulting universal coproduct identification takes $c\otimes1_X$ to $(i_0,i_1)$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison; extracted chain-interval foundation. Agent proof: Initial mapping complex and the coproduct identification from the stated adjunctions.

proof.text: Fix a cofibrant $X$ and any fibration $q:U\to V$ of $\mathcal N$. Apply the enriched model axiom ASSUMED IN THIS ITEM to the cofibration $O\to X$ and to $q$. By Step 3 its relative target is $0\times_0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,V)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,V)$. Consequently $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,q)$ is degreewise surjective, and it is a quasi-isomorphism when $q$ is a weak equivalence. By [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] it is therefore a fibration of complexes, and a trivial fibration when $q$ is a trivial fibration. This applies to arbitrary $U,V$, without their being fibrant. Here [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] supplies only the complex-enrichment conventions, not its diagram-model existence theorem with its stronger hypotheses.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison; extracted chain-interval foundation. Agent proof: The enriched axiom for the initial cofibration of X.

proof.text: To show that $(i_0,i_1)$ is a cofibration, take any square from this map to a trivial fibration $q:U\to V$. By the natural tensor adjunction and Step 3, this square is exactly a square of chain maps with left side $c:\mathbf Z[0]\oplus\mathbf Z[0]\to J$ and right side $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,q)$: its top map is the pair of adjoints of the two maps $X\to U$, and its bottom map is the adjoint of $J\otimes X\to V$. Step 2 makes $c$ a cofibration of complexes; Step 4 makes the right side a trivial fibration of complexes. The lifting axiom in the projective model of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] supplies a chain map $J\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,U)$ filling the square. Transposing it gives $J\otimes X\to U$, with both triangles commuting by naturality of the adjunction in [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. Thus $(i_0,i_1)$ lifts against every trivial fibration, so is a cofibration by the model-category lifting characterization.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison; extracted chain-interval foundation. Agent proof: The boundary lifting square for the specified tensor cylinder.

proof.text: Next take a square from $i_0:X\to J\otimes X$ to an arbitrary fibration $q:U\to V$. Under the same natural adjunction its left side becomes $j_0:\mathbf Z[0]\to J$ and its right side becomes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,q)$. Step 2 makes $j_0$ a trivial cofibration of complexes, and Step 4 makes the right side a fibration of complexes. The projective lifting axiom of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] supplies a chain-map filler $J\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,U)$; its adjoint fills the original square, by the natural adjunction of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. Hence $i_0$ lifts against every fibration and is a trivial cofibration in $\mathcal N$. This proves its weak-equivalence property directly, rather than assuming tensor preserves arbitrary weak equivalences.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison; extracted chain-interval foundation. Agent proof: The single-endpoint lifting square, using the contractible disk cokernel.

proof.text: The formulas in the statement give $pj_0=pj_1=1_{\mathbf Z[0]}$: on $1$ both composites have value $1$. Tensor functoriality and the unit identifications therefore give $p_Xi_0=p_Xi_1=1_X$. Since $i_0$ is a weak equivalence by Step 6 and $p_Xi_0=1_X$, two-out-of-three in the assumed model structure makes $p_X$ a weak equivalence. Together with Step 5 this is exactly the good-cylinder assertion. The only condition imposed on $X$ in the lifting argument was that $O\to X$ is a cofibration.
